<|channel|>analysis<|message|>We need to analyze each sentence to determine correctness.

We read the paper: It discusses cooperative perception system (Cooper). It mentions low-level fusion (raw data fusion), feature-level fusion, high-level fusion. It explains that high level fusion has disadvantages: it depends on the same object detection on each vehicle, missing objects can't be captured.

Look at technical details: In section 1 they mention that the cooperation uses raw data, LiDAR.

Now let's analyze each statement:

A. "The paper argues that late fusion has certain limitations in spatial alignment."

This statement references "late fusion" which is usually high-level fusion (object level). The paper talks about low-level fusion, feature-level fusion, high-level fusion. They discuss that high level fusion (also called late fusion?) isn't suitable because detection objects need shared object; failing to detect missing objects. In the paper, they mention "high level fusion is opted" etc. They mention "high level fusion is often opted over the other two levels of fusion due to being less complex, but this is not suitable for our needs. Object level relies too heavily on single vehicular sensors... This does not solve the issue of previously undetected objects, which will remain undetected even after fusion." They talk about spatial alignment around high-level fusion? It says "High level fusion: object detection results from each vehicle". They mention "some detection failures due to sensors blocked etc" meaning high-level fusion lacking. Does it mention spatial alignment? The paper says "low-level fusion, view from different vehicles, up into spatiotemporal alignment issues." But not sure. Perhaps they talk about mid-level fusion? Let's search: The text says "High level fusion is often opted over the other two levels of fusion due to being less complex, but this is not suitable for our needs. Object level relies too heavily on single vehicular sensors and will only work when both vehicles share a reference object in their detection. This does not solve the issue of previously undetected objects, which will remain undetected even after fusion. And thus, we turn our sights on the other two categories." They don't mention spatial alignment about late fusion. But maybe there is mention of "Late fusion" meaning feature-level or high-level? Not exactly. Let's see context: In Section 1.2 "B. Limitations of Prior Work" they say: "current state of multi-sensor fusion consists of three distinct categories: low level fusion, feature level fusion, and high level fusion. ... Each of these categories possess its own unique advantages and disadvantages. As their names imply, low level fusion consists of raw data fusion without any pre-processing done to the data ... Feature-level fusion takes the features extracted from the raw data before fusion. ... High level fusion takes the objects detected from each individual sensors... High level fusion is often opted over the other two levels of fusion due to being less complex, but this is not suitable for our needs. Object level relies too heavily on single vehicular sensors... This does not solve the issue..."

Thus, the statement "late fusion has certain limitations in spatial alignment" - is that correct? Which is "late fusion"? Possibly "late fusion" refers to high-level fusion: object-level vs raw data. And in the paper, they mention "four beam vs 64-beam" etc. They don't mention spatial alignment. But they mention that "high level fusion does not solve the issue of previously undetected objects." The question: "Which of the following statements is correct?" So we need to check if each statement is correct.

Option A: "The paper argues that late fusion has certain limitations in spatial alignment." I'm not fully sure if the paper says that. Perhaps the paper states "Late fusion" refers to high-level fusion, but the limitations are not exactly spatial alignment, but rather that it fails to detect unseen objects. The term "spatial alignment" is not used in the original text. They also mention "instead of fusion", may have mention of "dense point cloud", but not alignment. So I think A is not correct.

Option B: "The paper says that low-level fusion is more reliable than feature-level fusion." But the text says: "High level fusion is often opted over the other two levels of fusion due to being less complex, but this is not suitable for our needs. Object level relies too heavily on single vehicular sensors... This does not solve the issue of previously undetected objects, which will remain undetected even after fusion. And thus, we turn our sights on the other two categories." They didn't say that low-level fusion is more reliable than feature-level fusion. They just say they focus on low-level fusion. There is no mention that low-level is more reliable than feature-level. So B likely false.

Option C: "Although LiDAR has the advantage of spatial dimension, its disadvantage is that it cannot accurately perceive the license plate number." The paper says: "Based on the above reasons, we make a priority of these sensor data for cooperative sensing. We prefer LiDAR data because it holds advantage in providing location information... LiDAR point clouds have the advantage of spatial dimension over 2D images and video. Native obfuscation of entities or private data such as people’s faces and license plate numbers while preserving the accurate model of the perceived object. ... For image and LiDAR point clouds, ROI data will be extracted ... They say: "LiDAR point clouds have the advantage of spatial dimension... but for small object detection, for example license plate tracking, it is difficult for point clouds to recognize plate information." So they mention that LiDAR cannot precisely capture license plate numbers. So statement C says the disadvantage is that it cannot accurately perceive the license plate number. That matches PGP: The disadvantage is that LiDAR cannot detect license plate number. So C is correct.

Option D: "In our experiment, we only used GPS to test the robustness of the perception results." The paper says they test robustness of GPS reading drift. They mention they used GPS plus IMU. They also test using GPS and IMU skew times. They also mention they used GPS sensors to test. But they used GPS to test robustness. But the phrase "only used GPS to test the robustness of the perception results" is wrong because they also used IMU. So statement D is false.

Thus, the correct option is C. Let's test validity: The paper says "LiDAR point clouds... but for small object detection, e.g. license plate tracking, it is difficult for point clouds to recognize plate information." So that is mismatch: statement C says "LiDAR has advantage of spatial dimension, its disadvantage is that it cannot accurately perceive the license plate number." This matches. So C is correct.

Thus choose \boxed{C}.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>\boxed{C}
